identity.title: Dense Granule Protein DG9 of Cryptosporidium parvum Interacts With DG10 at the Dense Band.

content.abstract: Cryptosporidium parvum, a protozoan parasite, causes life-threatening diarrhea in young children and immunocompromised individuals. During host cell invasion and intracellular proliferation, C. parvum secretes rhoptry, dense granule (DG), and small granule (SG) proteins into the parasite-host interface. These secreted proteins facilitate the biogenesis of the parasitophorous vacuole (PV) enclosing the parasite and the feeder organelle and electron-dense band (DB) at the parasite-host interface. Nevertheless, the molecular compositions of these organelles are poorly defined. Here, we characterized the subcellular localization and functional role of cgd1_470, a highly polymorphic protein associated with host adaptation in the parasite. Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated endogenous tagging, we revealed that cgd1_470 is a novel DG protein, designated DG9. DG9 is secreted to the parasite-host interface during invasion and localizes to the DB after the PV formation. Deleting the dg9 gene did not significantly alter the in vitro growth or in vivo pathogenicity of a virulent C. parvum strain. Proteomic screening identified several putative DG9-interacting partners, including DG10 (cgd7_4280) and SG5 (cgd1_640), both of which display a similar interfacial localization. We validated the physical interaction between DG9 and DG10 using coimmunoprecipitation and colocalization analyses. Taken together, these findings suggest that DG9 and DG10 are interacting components of the DB at the parasite-host interface.
